ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC SDN List, and the Taiwan Ministry of Justice sanctions list. Additionally, screening against the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists is recommended. The screening must be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, immediate reporting to the FSC, and potential suspension of the incorporation process. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Online System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be registered as a transliteration or translation of the Chinese name. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) trade name, (2) business type, (3) organization type (e.g., Limited), and (4) additional designators. The Chinese name must be unique within the jurisdiction, and the English name must not be identical to any existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the original application, the rejection reason, and a revised name or justification. The MOEA will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Taipei High Administrative Court. The appeal process is governed by the Administrative Appeal Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally permissible for registration purposes; however, for a trade defense consulting company, tax authorities and banks may require a physical office presence to demonstrate commercial substance. The risk of rejection is moderate. It is recommended to secure a physical office to avoid challenges with tax registration and bank account opening, as virtual offices are often flagged for lacking operational substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered office is accessible during business hours; (2) Ensure that the company name is displayed at the entrance; (3) Maintain records of business transactions and contracts; (4) Have a designated person available for inspection. The likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection is low (estimated 10% annually) but increases if the municipality flags the company for tax irregularities or if the registered address is a virtual office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 18, 98-113, 128-131 where applicable, and Articles 387-393; Foreign Investment Act Articles 4, 8, and 9; Business Registration Act; and Regulations Governing Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent company registration authority for the registered-office location, generally the relevant municipal or county/city government economic development department; the Ministry of Economic Affairs Commercial Development Administration handles matters within its statutory jurisdiction.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration, accompanied by the company articles of incorporation, shareholder and director information, capital verification documents, registered-office evidence, and foreign-investment approval documents where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum capital for a limited company, except where a special regulated business requires one. The subscribed capital must be fully paid before registration, and a Taiwan-certified public accountant must verify the capital. A foreign investor must obtain investment approval, remit funds through an approved bank, and complete capital verification and investment realization procedures. No general escrow account is required, but funds must remain traceable through the designated bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and record the subscription by each approved shareholder for the shares and capital stated in the incorporation documents, subject to applicable foreign-investment approval and capital verification. RESOLVED, that the registered office at [Taiwan address] be adopted with effect from incorporation. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Chairperson, [name] be appointed Director, and [name] be appointed Manager, each authorized to execute incorporation filings, banking mandates, tax registrations, employment arrangements, and licensing applications. RESOLVED, that the officers may take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions and maintain statutory books and records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Permitted Business Scope and Corporate Form
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion, and the competent company registration authority for the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the proposed activities are accurately described in the business scope. Separate general trade-remedy consulting from reserved attorney services, court representation, and legal opinions on Taiwan law. Because the payload describes a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, confirm the intended Taiwan legal form; Taiwan does not use the PRC-specific equity-joint-venture form. Use a Taiwan limited company unless another legally available structure is approved.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese and English company names
Proposed business items and industry codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the business items, corporate form, ownership structure, or proposed company name in response to a written query and resubmit through the same authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Items
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company One-Stop Registration system or the competent municipal/county/city company registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Chinese company name and proposed business items electronically. Check name similarity, restricted words, and regulated-business classifications. Pay the applicable name reservation fee. Do not represent that the company may provide Taiwan-law attorney services unless the relevant attorney and professional-entity requirements are satisfied.
required_dossiers: Applicant identity or corporate registration documents
Foreign investor power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace rejected names or amend business items and resubmit; preserve the application reference and respond to any deficiency notice within the stated cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application before capital remittance or capitalization. Provide the investment plan, ownership chain, ultimate beneficial-owner information, investor resolutions, powers of attorney, and proposed company documents. Authenticate, notarize, and legalize foreign documents as required, with certified Chinese translations. Remit approved capital through a Taiwan bank and retain bank certificates.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation or equivalent
Foreign investor board or shareholder resolution
Notarized and legalized documents with Chinese translations
Draft articles of incorporation and shareholder list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer supplemental-information requests, correct ownership or investment-plan inconsistencies, and request administrative review or appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act if a final adverse decision is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-certified public accountant and the competent company registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of incorporation and shareholder subscription documents. Open the preparatory bank account, remit the approved capital, obtain bank evidence, and commission a Taiwan-certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report. Complete notarization or certification where required by the filing office or document origin.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the capital amount, remittance trail, signatures, or accountant report; obtain a revised verification report before filing incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company One-Stop Registration system or the competent municipal/county/city company registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application and all supporting documents electronically or in paper form. Pay the applicable registration fee, which is generally NT$700 online or NT$1,000 for paper filing, subject to current fee schedules. Ensure the registered office is legally usable and that the articles, shareholder list, director appointments, capital verification, and foreign-investment approval are consistent.
required_dossiers: Powers of attorney and legalized foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the deficiency notice, replace defective documents, pay any additional fee, and resubmit within the prescribed cure period. A formal refusal may be challenged through administrative appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Tax, Banking, and Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau branch, Taiwan bank, labor authorities, and the competent company registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the company registration certificate, activate the corporate bank account, complete tax registration and invoice setup, and maintain statutory accounting books, shareholder registers, director records, and beneficial-ownership information. File any post-investment realization report and register amendments within statutory deadlines. Register employees for labor and health insurance where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or registry discrepancies through the responsible office, file late amendments where permitted, and pay applicable penalties or surcharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: For general business registration: the competent municipal or county/city economic development authority. For regulated attorney services: the Ministry of Justice, the relevant local bar association, and the Taiwan Bar Association under the Attorneys Act. No general manufacturing licensing board applies to an office-based anti-dumping consultancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Company Registration and Business Registration; additionally, Attorney Practice Registration or permitted foreign-legal-affairs registration where the business provides reserved attorney services, legal representation, or Taiwan-law legal advice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Ministry of Environment, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based consulting with no construction, manufacturing, prescribed facility, or significant environmental impact.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, industrial-air-emission, or hazardous-production-waste authorization is ordinarily applicable to a normal office. The company must use licensed waste contractors where regulated waste is generated, comply with the Waste Disposal Act, prevent improper discharge, and comply with local sewer and building requirements. Any future laboratory, warehouse, manufacturing, fuel, chemical, or substantial construction activity requires a new environmental screening.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain landlord and building-management confirmation that the premises are approved for office use. Comply with the Fire Services Act, applicable building and fire codes, evacuation and emergency-planning requirements, and any inspection required by the local fire department. Structural-load certification is generally unnecessary for ordinary office occupancy but may be required for alterations, heavy equipment, archives, or changed use. Comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, labor insurance, health insurance, workplace risk controls, and mandatory training. No factory occupational clearance is required unless physical industrial operations are added.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; integrated e-Tax portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw; electronic invoice platform: https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw. Regional NTA offices (e.g., Taipei National Taxation Administration) administer local tax registration and audits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in the form of a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise limited company obtains an 8-digit Unified Business Number (UBIN), which serves as the statutory TIN and VAT registration number. Procedural steps: (1) foreign investment screening and approval by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), if applicable under the Foreign Investment Negative List; (2) filing of company incorporation and business registration with MOEA; (3) automatic forwarding of registration data by MOEA to the National Taxation Administration under the integrated company/tax registration process; (4) issuance of the UBIN and Tax Registration Certificate by the NTA; (5) registration of electronic Uniform Invoice issuance through the NTA electronic invoice integration service platform; and (6) if the JV has no place of fixed business in Taiwan, application for VAT registration with the local National Taxation Administration branch or through online tax SaaS channels.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The JV is a resident profit-seeking enterprise taxable in Taiwan on its worldwide income at the corporate income tax rate of 20%; undistributed earnings are subject to the 5% retained earnings surtax. It is not a pass-through entity; no partnership flow-through or check-the-box pass-through election is available. Foreign shareholders' dividends are generally subject to withholding tax at source unless reduced by an applicable double tax treaty or the Taiwan Offshore Banking Unit regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a check-the-box election for entity classification; the JV is mandatorily classified as an entity-level taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and the Business Tax Act. In limited cases, the JV may make statutory elections or invoke relief mechanisms, including: (i) election of the foreign income tax credit for foreign-source income under Article 3 of the Income Tax Act, subject to the creditable limit in Taiwan; (ii) application of double tax treaty benefits, including reduced withholding rates and mutual agreement procedure; (iii) election to file as a regular VAT zero-rated exporter for input VAT refund purposes; and (iv) adoption of the Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) filing posture under the Income Basic Tax Act where applicable. No hybrid mismatch or group consolidation elections are recognized under Taiwan tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (VAT), statutorily referred to in Taiwan as Business Tax (營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The mandatory VAT/GST registration threshold is average monthly taxable sales exceeding NT$200,000 in the preceding six months. A business falling below this threshold may nonetheless register voluntarily. Once registered, the enterprise must issue Uniform Invoices and file quarterly business tax returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan enforces an electronic Uniform Invoice (統一發票) system. VAT-registered enterprises must issue e-invoices through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integrated Service Platform (EIIP) and transmit invoice data to the platform within 48 hours of issuance. There is no pre-clearance or real-time digital stamping authorization by the tax authority; compliance is achieved through post-issuance electronic transmission, barcode/QR code coding, and matching of B2B invoice data with buyers' Unified Business Numbers. Export zero-rated invoices must be separately coded and filed as 0% tax rate in the quarterly Business Tax return. The API-based EIIP supports B2B and B2C cloud invoice issuance, electronic storage, buyer system integration, and automatic audit trail generation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act. For the JV's trade-remedy defense consulting services (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541199), zero-rating applies where services are provided to foreign enterprises or individuals and are actually used outside Taiwan, including anti-dumping and trade defense consulting performed from Taiwan for overseas clients. Export of goods similarly qualifies at 0% where customs export formalities are completed. The zero-rating claim is effected by stating the 0% rate in the quarterly Business Tax return and retaining documentary proof of exportation or foreign service use. Unlike tax-exempt sales, zero-rated sales allow recovery of input VAT, and excess input VAT is refundable to the exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (出口結匯水單/外匯收入水單)
Sales Contract or Purchase Order (買賣契約書/訂單)
Service Performance Evidence for Cross-Border Services (e.g., service report, correspondence, offshore use certification, and foreign client identification)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Administration cross-checks zero-rating claims against customs export declarations, banking FX records, and electronic invoice data. Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating claims cause restoration of the 5% VAT and disallowance of input VAT credits, plus interest. Under the Business Tax Act, tax evasion or misclassification may result in a penalty of up to 5 times the underpaid tax; grossly fraudulent filings may also trigger criminal liability, TIN de-registration, denial of refund privilege, and blacklisting of the responsible legal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Primary authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) exercising administration of RMB and foreign-currency accounts for the domestic JV. Ancillary authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) governs Taiwan-dollar settlement and cross-strait fund flows to the extent TW-source funds are routed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current-account transactions (consultancy fees, legal-defense service remittances) are generally freely convertible upon production of genuine transaction documents, under the 1996 IMF Article VIII obligations and the PRC Foreign Exchange Regulations; capital-account items (FDI equity injection, shareholder loans, liquidation remittances) require SAFE or bank-level registration and do not enjoy automatic convertibility. Profit remittance requires an audited financial statement, board profit-distribution resolution, tax assessment/payment certificates, and prior foreign-exchange registration; no general remittance cap is imposed for qualifying reinvestment of RMB profits, but Taiwan-dollar capital repatriation must be supported by a completed asset inspection report (验资报告). The JV's business is a professional-services exporter, so its primary convertibility risk lies in proving the 'real need' of each USD/TWD payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory blanket surrender of service-trade export proceeds was abolished; the JV may retain eligible export/non-trade current-account income in a foreign-currency account or sell it to a designated bank at commercial rates. Statutory compliance obligations under SAFE include (i) filing of the cross-border service-trade contract with the bank; (ii) submission of receipt/payment application and underlying invoices through the bank's Service-Trade FX administration system; and (iii) repatriation of service income within the banking period and no delayed offshore accumulation absent a SAFE-approved offshore account. For trade-remedy consulting, the bank will classify receipts as 'Consultancy and related services' with the appropriate SAFE purpose code (e.g., 4241 or 4242), and no fixed statutory surrender ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital-Pledge Foreign Exchange Account (Capital Account) + RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Generally Low for this JV structure. Offshore digital bank/EMI providers (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, TransferWise/Revolut) cannot maintain RMB-denominated onshore accounts or accept SAFE-regulated capital injections; they may only serve as inbound collection gateways for small-value service invoices through licensed partner banks in China. For statutory capital injection, LC operations, or large trade-defense disbursements, a physical mainland bank account remains mandatory. If the JV chooses an EMI corridor, SAFE will still require the ultimate onshore bank settlement record and full underlying contract data, making the marginal compliance benefit negligible except for micro-consulting receivables.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBOC/SAFE practice, initial opening of a corporate account for a foreign-invested JV does not require all directors to travel, but the legal representative (or a licensed proxy appointed by notarized power of attorney) must appear in person at a designated bank branch for identity interview and photo capture. For a cross-border JV with Taiwan shareholders, banks commonly require a remote video interview with each director owning more than 10% equity, plus submission of corporate resolutions certified by the company secretary and notarized copies of the articles of association. Pure online/remote account opening is not generally available for accounts receiving foreign equity; physical attendance, either by the legal representative or a senior executive proxy, remains the practical requirement for BOC and ICBC under their 'Double Interview' rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder structure includes an offshore intermediate holding company (Hong Kong/BVI) with no apparent commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE/PBOC UBO declaration; corporate registry excerpt and shareholders register; beneficial-ownership chain up to natural persons; audited financial statements of intermediate entities; explanation of reasons for intermediate holding with a legal opinion from mainland counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Paid-in capital injected from Taiwan may be viewed as high-risk cross-strait fund movement subject to CBC/SAFE double surveillance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed SAFE FDI registration form; Taiwan Central Bank cross-strait remittance approval/notification where applicable; bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation; investment contract with valuation certificate; capital-contribution schedule; board minutes and tax registration in both jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal-defense consulting fees invoiced to a foreign defendant, not a mainland resident, may raise suspicion of round-tripping or tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed legal-services agreements with clear fee clause; portfolio of anti-dumping case filings and procedural submissions; itemized invoices with hours and disbursements; engagement letter from trade-remedy attorney; evidence of actual delivery (e-mails, court/agency filings); bank-level transactional narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outbound payments to overseas anti-dumping counsel (legal retainers) without a registered service-trade contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Outbound contracts registered with the tax bureau under tax-clearance filing; cross-border service-trade declaration (Form F.30.4); payment proof covering exactly the boarded fees; invoices from foreign counsel; legal-residence/tax numbers of overseas counsel; proper SAFE purpose code (e.g., 4241 or 4242 for legal/consulting services).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Sino-Foreign Equity JV, the compliant inbound wire is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan shareholder's NT$/USD account to the bank-designated FDI Capital-Pledge Account in mainland China. The remittance instruction must carry (i) an accurate Purpose of Payment code, normally '623011 - Capital contribution for establishment of foreign-invested enterprise' or '623012 - Increase in paid-in capital of a foreign-invested enterprise'; (ii) a clear reference to the SAFE FDI registration number (业务编号); and (iii) the beneficiary bank's 12-digit SWIFT BIC. Before disbursement, the bank screens the remitter name against the SAFE investment record, obtains the company passport/credential and FIE business license, and verifies the capital contribution through a capital-account 'foreign-exchange settlement' process. The JV must not use the basic RMB account for inbound foreign-exchange capital; any attempt to send equity proceeds via an ordinary operational remittance will be recalled or blocked.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-defense consulting outflows predominately clear via SWIFT MT103 (bank wire) with a custom 'Services / Legal Fees' purpose code (e.g., China SAFE Service-Trade Code 4241/4242), supported by (i) a cross-border service-trade contract; (ii) a tax-withholding certificate or tax-exemption certificate filed with the local State Tax Bureau; and (iii) an electronic service-trade declaration in the bank's cross-border payment system. For larger tariff-rate or trade-remedy campaign expenses, a Commercial Letter of Credit is not structurally advisable because legal retainers are not deliverable goods; where a foreign anti-dumping authority demands a guarantee, a standby L/C (SWIFT MT760) issued by BOC to a Taiwan/Korea/Europe beneficiary can be used, but the ordinary operative rail is a cleared SWIFT wire through admitted CNY/USD/TWD channels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (CNY/USD and CNY/EUR) against genuine current-account service-trade receivables and payables
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (CNY/USD, CNY/TWD, USD/TWD) with licensed bank counterparties
FX options (call/put on USD/CNY, USD/TWD) where the notional is capped by SAFE real-demand underlying amounts
Short-term currency deposits in CNY, USD, and TWD to reduce conversion-timing risk
Onshore RMB NDFs are not permissible; where TWD hedging is required, use a deliverable USD/TWD forward at Bank of Taiwan or an offshore branch acting under SAFE real-demand rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Major Shareholder and Beneficial Owner List Filing (Companies Act Art. 22-1; 年度股東及最終受益人申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office via the e-Government corporate registry portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after each calendar year-end, i.e., by January 15 of the following year; mid-year changes in 10% or greater shareholding must be reported within 15 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rectification order followed by administrative fine of NT$50,000 to NT$5,000,000 per violation (Companies Act Art. 22-1); persistent non-compliance supports compulsory deregistration and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Undistributed Retained Earnings Surtax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報暨未分配盈餘申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 of the year following the calendar tax year; the 5% surtax on undistributed retained earnings is declared on the same return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (subject to statutory caps) plus daily interest for failure to file timely; failure to file after formal notice triggers a higher failure-to-file surcharge, and fraudulent underreporting may be penalized by up to three times the underpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Income Tax Installment (暫繳營利事業所得稅申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By September 30 each year covering the first half of the calendar year; a second optional installment may be filed by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid provisional tax accrues interest at the overdue-tax rate plus a delinquency surcharge; continued default leads to enforced collection against registered company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Convening and Adoption of Audited Financial Statements and Profit-Distribution Proposal (股東常會)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (corporate organ); minutes retained as a statutory corporate record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by June 30 for a calendar-year company (Companies Act Art. 170)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA may order directors to convene within a specified period and impose administrative fines of up to NT$500,000 on responsible persons; sustained default can result in compulsory deregistration and loss of legal existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Post-AGM Filing of Adopted Financial Statements, Profit Appropriation or Distribution Resolution, and Meeting Minutes with MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements (Companies Act Art. 230)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$10,000 to NT$500,000 on the responsible company for non-filing or delayed filing (Companies Act Art. 230 and Art. 183); repeated default may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Corporate Secretarial Compliance Certificate (internal statutory deliverable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and the company secretary or corporate governance officer; documented basis for the Art. 22-1 certification to MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed during the annual financial close by March 31, matching the deadline for the board to prepare statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine; material register defects discovered during MOEA inspection or Investment Commission review trigger rectification orders, fines, and adverse findings that impede dividend remittances and professional license renewals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit and certification is triggered when paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or more, when outstanding credit facilities from financial institutions reach NT$30 million or more, or when the company is designated by MOEA or the Financial Supervisory Commission (Companies Act Art. 20); foreign-invested JV companies seeking to remit dividends, implement capital reductions, or register shareholder transfers must in practice furnish audited financial statements to the MOEA Investment Commission upon application. Companies below the thresholds may file CPA-reviewed or compiled financial statements unless a lending bank or a foreign investor agreement requires a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Business Entity Accounting Act (商業會計法), Financial Reporting Standards for Enterprises (企業會計準則公報; IFRS-for-SMEs-based local GAAP) for non-public companies, and IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission for public companies; the annual financial report comprises balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, cash flows, and notes, maintained in New Taiwan Dollars; statutory books and important vouchers must be retained for at least 10 years, ordinary vouchers for at least 5 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Companies Act Art. 22-1, the JV must maintain a current register of shareholders and identified ultimate beneficial owners and file the register with MOEA by January 15 each year; any transfer resulting in a 10% or greater beneficial ownership change must be reported within 15 days of the transfer. The company secretary must obtain a signed UBO declaration (name, national ID or passport, and ownership percentage) from each shareholder upon admission, upon each transfer, and during the annual confirmation cycle; failure to identify a natural-person UBO makes the reported corporate chain presumptively non-compliant.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors (董事及監察人名冊)
Shareholders' and Board Meeting Minutes Book (議事錄)
Major Shareholder and Beneficial Owner Register (主要股東及最終受益人登記簿)
Company Seal, Certificate, and License Book (印鑑及證照簿)
Accounting Books and Vouchers Archive (帳簿及會計憑證)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 to 1,200 per annum (NT$10,000 to 35,000) for registered-office address and corporate secretarial agency service, including register custody, e-portal filing support, and company seal custody
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to 7,500 per annum (NT$80,000 to 240,000) for a full statutory CPA audit of a small to mid-size trade-defense consulting JV; USD 1,000 to 2,500 for a CPA-review compilation when below the mandatory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax; the first NT$120,000 of taxable income is effectively exempt under the progressive formula in Income Tax Act Article 5(5))
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 20% headline with effective zero-rate on the first NT$120,000 taxable income; R&D investment tax credit up to 10% of qualifying expenditure (Industrial Innovation Act); foreign tax credit on cross-border trade-defense income; 5% retained-earnings surtax that incentivizes annual dividend distribution; no preferential rate for foreign-owned entities or export-consulting revenue
